core_obligations: Set up the criterion (proof lines 5315-5320): the lemma follows if every pro-etale covering of V can be refined to one whose members admit no morphism into U over X, since the sections of the extension by zero are computed as a colimit over such coverings; refine first to a finite covering with affine members.

Build a refining covering (proof lines 5320-5326): for each member V_i = Spec(A_i) let Z_i be the inverse image of Z and set W_i = Spec(A_{i,Z_i}^tilde); the map from the disjoint union of the W_i to V is weakly etale, and its image contains all points of V_Z, hence by the specialization assumption contains all points of V, so {W_i -> V} is a pro-etale covering refining the given one.

Conclude (proof lines 5326-5329): every point of W_i specializes to a point lying over Z, and since U meets Z trivially in X there can be no morphism W_i -> U over X; the criterion of the first step therefore gives the vanishing of the sections of the extension by zero.
proof_roadmap: Refine an arbitrary pro-etale covering to a finite covering by affines.
Replace each member by the localization at its closed part over Z, which still covers by the specialization assumption.
Conclude that the refined members admit no morphism into the open part, hence the extension by zero has no sections.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a weakly etale morphism j : U -> X, a closed immersion i : Z -> X disjoint from U and an affine object V of the pro-etale site all of whose points specialize into V_Z, the extension by zero of any abelian sheaf on U has no sections over V (statement lines 5306-5313). The proof (proof lines 5315-5331) refines a given covering to a finite affine one, replaces each member by the localization at its part over Z so that the refinement still covers by the specialization hypothesis, and concludes that no member admits a morphism into U. H2: a three-step refinement argument with two inputs, written out in full.
